executiveSummary.text: Regime: late-cycle risk-on is being stress-tested by a hawkish Fed shock, not a broad de-risking yet: S&P 500 -0.45%, Nasdaq roughly flat, Dow -1.21%, VIX 17.7, DXY +0.69%, 10Y Treasury about 5.01%.

Fed hiked 25 bp to 3.75%-4.00% and signalled a faster return to 2% inflation; 2Y/10Y/30Y Treasury yields are about 4.74%/5.01%/5.35%. This is a discount-rate shock for long-duration AI, REITs and gold.

AI/semis held up better than expected despite higher yields: QQQ +0.03%, TSM +0.96%, NVDA +0.82%, ASML +0.67%; Synopsys +2.93% was the only near-threshold KL move and likely reflects AI/EDA resilience rather than thesis-changing news.

Oil fell sharply from war-risk levels: WTI -3.6%, Brent -2.9% after reports a damaged Saudi pipeline could restart within days, while Hormuz traffic remains severely impaired. This lowers immediate inflation impulse but keeps the energy tail risk alive.

Singapore stayed defensive: STI ended -0.1% at 5,635.41; DBS +0.1%, OCBC +0.6%, UOB -0.3%. Bank dividend yields now screen below average S-REIT yields, but higher global yields cap REIT re-rating speed.

usGlobal.what: US equities absorbed a Fed hike unevenly: Nasdaq flat, S&P modestly lower, Dow hit harder.
usGlobal.why: Higher yields and stronger USD pressure duration and cyclicals, but AI/semis retained buyers.
usGlobal.implication: Do not read this as broad capitulation; it is rotation plus discount-rate repricing.

ratesMacro.what: Fed raised policy rate 25 bp to 3.75%-4.00% and bond yields jumped at the front/intermediate end.
ratesMacro.why: The Fed message prioritised a timelier inflation return, lifting real-rate/terminal-rate expectations.
ratesMacro.implication: Raises hurdle rates for AI capex, REITs and gold; supports KL cash optionality.

asiaSingapore.what: STI slipped 0.1%; DBS +0.1%, OCBC +0.6%, UOB -0.3%; S-REIT average yields screen above bank yields in local commentary.
asiaSingapore.why: Singapore banks remain quality income compounders, but valuation/yield compression is visible; REITs need falling yields to unlock rerating.
asiaSingapore.implication: Hold banks; add REIT exposure only selectively on yield-spike weakness, not on generic yield-chasing.

commodities.what: Oil dropped ~3% while gold softened and copper rose.
commodities.why: Saudi pipeline restart hopes eased immediate supply shock; higher USD/real yields weighed on gold; copper is still supported by electrification/grid scarcity.
commodities.implication: Energy inflation tail is reduced but not removed; scarcity basket remains a strategic hedge, not a straight-line trade.

geopolitics.what: Hormuz shipping traffic reportedly remains at a fraction of normal even as oil sold off on supply-restoration headlines.
geopolitics.why: Markets are pricing lower near-term outage probability but not full normalization of chokepoint risk.
geopolitics.implication: Transmission path is oil -> inflation expectations -> Fed path -> equity multiples; watch shipping normalization, not headlines alone.

moves.what: No KL individual holding breached the +/-3% abnormal-move threshold; no KL ETF breached +/-1.5%. Synopsys was close at +2.93%.
moves.why: AI/EDA and semicap quality factors remained bid despite higher yields; no fresh thesis-damaging news found in last-24h scan.
moves.implication: Portfolio AI sleeve is acting resiliently, but higher real yields can compress multiples if earnings revisions do not accelerate.
moves.action: HOLD; WATCH SNPS only if it clears +3% on company-specific news or if EDA re-rating becomes crowded.

moves.what: KL energy-linked scarcity exposures were mixed: COPX -0.47%, URNM -0.36%, GLD -0.61%, SLV -0.83%; oil itself fell >2% but KL does not hold direct oil futures.
moves.why: USD/yield strength offset scarcity narrative; oil supply-restoration headlines cooled inflation panic.
moves.implication: Do not extrapolate one-day commodity softness into broken scarcity thesis; the causal driver is rates/USD and supply headline, not demand destruction yet.
moves.action: HOLD; ADD only on forced liquidations or when real yields stop rising.

thesisImpact.what: AI scarcity thesis intact but discount-rate sensitivity has increased.
thesisImpact.why: Semis/EDA are still fundamental bottlenecks; Fed/higher yields raise valuation hurdle.
thesisImpact.implication: Prefer toll-road quality and profitable bottlenecks over speculative AI beta.
thesisImpact.action: HOLD/ADD on drawdowns; invalidator is AI capex cuts spreading from hyperscalers to equipment orders.

thesisImpact.what: Singapore income sleeve remains ballast, not high-growth engine.
thesisImpact.why: Banks are expensive on yield relative to REITs; REITs need lower yields but offer higher carry.
thesisImpact.implication: Keep banks as quality ballast; selectively accumulate REITs only when spreads compensate for rate risk.
thesisImpact.action: HOLD banks; WATCH REITs for 10Y yield rollover.

narratives.title: Fed credibility over asset reflation
narratives.description: The market is repricing the Fed as willing to tighten despite elevated long-end yields. First order: stronger USD and higher front-end yields. Second order: tighter global liquidity for EM/Asia and higher equity discount rates. Third order: only companies with pricing power and visible cash flows keep valuation support.
narratives.source: NPR/Yahoo/NYT Fed live coverage, last 24h; Treasury H.15
narratives.priceImpact: negative for duration; mixed for quality cash-flow equities

narratives.title: AI infrastructure remains the market's quality growth refuge
narratives.description: Semis and EDA did not break under a rate shock, implying investors still differentiate AI bottlenecks from generic growth. The risk is not today’s price action; it is whether higher rates force hyperscalers to slow capex later.
narratives.source: Yahoo price data and last-24h semiconductor news scan
narratives.priceImpact: constructive if earnings revisions persist; vulnerable if capex guidance softens

narratives.title: Oil risk is about inflation path, not a simple geopolitics trade
narratives.description: Oil fell on pipeline-restart news even with Hormuz traffic impaired. First order: lower crude eases inflation fears. Second order: if shipping remains constrained, insurance/freight and refined-product stress can reappear. Third order: Fed may stay hawkish if energy shocks leak into inflation expectations.
narratives.priceImpact: near-term oil lower; medium-term inflation risk unresolved

secondOrderEffects.text: Higher 2Y/10Y yields raise the discount rate for AI and REITs; if AI earnings revisions keep rising, quality semis can still outperform, but REITs need yield relief to re-rate.
secondOrderEffects.implication: Add to AI bottlenecks only on valuation resets; be patient with REITs.

secondOrderEffects.text: Stronger USD tightens global financial conditions; USD/SGD strength slightly reduces SGD value of foreign assets only if unhedged translation is favourable, but it pressures Asia risk appetite.
secondOrderEffects.implication: KL’s global USD assets get translation support; Asia/EM beta deserves caution.

secondOrderEffects.text: Oil falling reduces immediate CPI pressure, but if Hormuz/shipping constraints persist, refined products and freight costs can transmit inflation later.
secondOrderEffects.implication: Watch oil curves and shipping volumes, not just spot crude.

investment.thesis: Keep the AI scarcity barbell: TSM/ASML/LRCX/AMAT/KLAC/SNPS/AVGO plus grid/copper/uranium as bottlenecks that AI physically depends on.
investment.trigger: Add in tranches on 8-12% sleeve drawdowns or when order books/capex guidance remain intact despite rate volatility.
investment.whyNow: Rate shock is testing multiples, but fundamental bottlenecks remain scarce.
investment.invalidator: Hyperscaler capex cuts become broad and equipment/EDA order revisions turn negative.

investment.thesis: Preserve KL’s cash/CPF/property ballast as strategic optionality toward SGD 3M liquid FI target.
investment.trigger: Deploy only when expected 5-year IRR beats cash by a wide margin or panic creates quality mispricing.
investment.whyNow: Cash at ~4% is valuable when Fed hawkishness raises volatility.
investment.invalidator: Real yields collapse and broad risk assets reset to attractive forward returns.

trading.thesis: Avoid chasing REIT rallies until the US 10Y clearly rolls over below ~4.75% or Singapore REIT spreads widen enough to compensate.
trading.trigger: US 10Y <4.75% for several sessions plus stabilising USD/SGD.
trading.whyNow: Current 5% 10Y yield caps duration-sensitive income assets.
trading.invalidator: REIT earnings/NAV deterioration or credit spreads widen.

trading.thesis: Oil shock fade is tactical only; do not short scarcity structurally while Hormuz traffic remains impaired.
trading.trigger: Shipping normalizes toward pre-crisis levels and Brent breaks below US$100 with inventories rebuilding.
trading.whyNow: Spot crude sold off on pipeline restart hopes, but chokepoint data remain stressed.
trading.invalidator: Renewed attacks, insurance spike, or Brent reclaims recent highs.

watchlist.thesis: AI capex revision risk is the key portfolio swing factor.
watchlist.trigger: MSFT/AMZN/GOOG/META guide capex lower or push out data-center projects.
watchlist.whyNow: Higher rates make capex discipline more likely at the margin.
watchlist.invalidator: Backlog and capex guidance accelerate further.

watchlist.thesis: USD/liquidity stress could turn a rate shock into broader risk-off.
watchlist.trigger: DXY >102, VIX >22, credit spreads widen, USD/JPY carry volatility rises.
watchlist.whyNow: Dollar strength is the main cross-asset tightening channel.
watchlist.invalidator: DXY reverses and yields fall without growth scare.

riskWatch.name: Fed/real-yield overshoot
riskWatch.description: A hawkish Fed plus 5% 10Y can compress long-duration multiples and slow capex-sensitive sectors.
riskWatch.mitigation: Keep cash dry powder; add only to high-quality bottlenecks on valuation resets.

riskWatch.name: Energy chokepoint/inflation feedback
riskWatch.description: Oil fell, but Hormuz traffic remains reportedly far below normal; renewed supply stress could lift inflation expectations and delay rate relief.
riskWatch.mitigation: Maintain diversified scarcity exposure; avoid overconcentration in rate-sensitive assets.

riskWatch.name: AI crowding/earnings gap
riskWatch.description: Semis holding up in a rate shock is positive, but crowded positioning leaves downside if capex or margins disappoint.
riskWatch.mitigation: Prefer profitable toll roads; avoid chasing single-name spikes.

keyEvents.text: Fed hiked 25 bp to 3.75%-4.00%; yields and USD rose.
US 2Y/10Y/30Y Treasury curve: 4.74% / 5.01% / 5.35% on Sep 16 Treasury data.
Singapore STI closed -0.1% at 5,635.41; banks mixed.
WTI/Brent fell about 3% after reports damaged Saudi pipeline could restart in days; Hormuz traffic still impaired.

bottomLine.whatMatters: The main regime driver is not equity weakness; it is higher rates/USD testing whether AI earnings power can outrun discount-rate pressure.
bottomLine.whatToDo: Hold core AI bottlenecks and Singapore ballast; keep cash optionality; add only on high-quality drawdowns or clear yield relief.
bottomLine.whatToIgnore: Ignore one-day commodity/gold narratives and generic crisis heuristics; follow real yields, USD, shipping normalization and hyperscaler capex guidance. Probability view: 50% choppy risk-on rotation, 30% broader rate-led correction, 20% oil/geopolitical inflation shock. Confidence: medium.
